title: Perfectly Inelastic Collision in One Dimension
theory:
**Big idea:** The bodies stick together. Momentum gives the common velocity, and some kinetic energy is always lost.

**Final velocity**
m₁v₁ + m₂v₂ = (m₁ + m₂) V
**V = (m₁v₁ + m₂v₂) / (m₁ + m₂)**

**Loss in kinetic energy**
**ΔK = m₁m₂ (v₁ – v₂)² / [2 (m₁ + m₂)]**
This is always **positive**: kinetic energy is lost, turning into heat, sound and deformation.

**🧮 Worked example: carts moving towards each other**
A 50 kg cart at 20 km/h meets a 20 kg cart coming the other way at 10 km/h. They cling together.
(50)(20) – (20)(10) = 70 V, so **V = 80/7 ≈ 11.4 km/h**, in the 50 kg cart's direction.

**🧮 Worked example: energy lost**
A 1 kg block at 2 m/s sticks to a 1 kg block at rest.
V = 1 m/s. ΔK = (1 × 1 × 4) / (2 × 2) = **1 J**, half the original 2 J.

> ⚠️ **Common mistake:** Forgetting the minus sign for a body moving the **other way**.

questions.prompt: After a perfectly inelastic collision, the common velocity is:
questions.explanation: Momentum conservation with v₁′ = v₂′ = V.

questions.prompt: A 50 kg cart moving at 20 km/h collides with a 20 kg cart coming towards it at 10 km/h, and they stick together. Their common speed is about:
The loss of kinetic energy in a perfectly inelastic collision is:

options.text: Equal to the initial kinetic energy

questions.prompt: A 1 kg block moving at 2 m/s sticks to an identical block at rest. The kinetic energy lost is:
The kinetic energy lost in a perfectly inelastic collision mostly turns into:
questions.explanation: The energy is not destroyed. It changes into internal energy and sound.
